notes: Identity independently verified from supplied text: matching title Young Adults’ Fertility Expectations and Events: Associations With College Enrollment and Persistence; authors R Kelly Raley, Yujin Kim, Kimberly Daniels; J Marriage Fam. 2012 Aug;74(4):866–879; DOI 10.1111/j.1741-3737.2012.00990.x; PMCID PMC3665345. PMC author-manuscript full primary report with Method, Results, Tables 1–5, Discussion and references; not an abstract-only or secondary article. No PDF supplied, so printed page 8 cannot be mapped from this unpaginated web text. Description and original locator are blank; no outcome, predictor, sample or model is supplied. No assignment by row order or numeric resemblance. Candidate Ns only for parent field-scope review: Table 2 college attendance N=7,838 participants; Table 3 college attendance n=3,062 participants age 15+ in 1997; Table 5 four-year dropout n=2,605 individuals contributing 96,871 person-month observations. Method also gives 1,962 two-year college respondents. Enrollment analysis excludes marriage/pregnancy before leaving high school and requires an interview after high school; persistence excludes marriage, birth or cohabitation at first enrollment; Table 3 additionally restricts to respondents age 15+ in 1997 for college-expectations eligibility. Missing independent variables are multiply imputed. No model is uniquely assigned, so none of these is promoted to target analytic N. No sum and no inference from df. Illustrative focal candidates, not an exhaustive list of predictors: Table 2 fertility expectation, two-year versus no college, RRR 0.96 (printed B −0.05, SE 0.01, ** = p < .01); four-year versus no college, RRR 0.91 (B −0.09, SE 0.02, *** = p < .001). Table 3 fertility expectation without college-expectations control: two-year RRR 0.97 (B −0.03, SE 0.02, no star; numeric p not established), four-year RRR 0.89 (B −0.11, SE 0.03, p < .01); with that control: two-year RRR 0.99 (B −0.01, SE 0.02, no star; numeric p not established), four-year RRR 0.93 (B −0.07, SE 0.03, p < .05). RRR is explicitly relative risk ratio; fertility expectations explicitly scaled per 10 percentage-point change in perceived probability. Printed RRRs retained without conversion or reconciliation with B. Many other predictors also have RRRs. Requested metric cannot select the outcome, predictor or model. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders; replication source not supplied or inspected.
